before.known: आपके जाने के बाद मेरे पास कुछ नहीं बचा।
before.target: I've got nothing left after you left

after.known: आपके जाने के बाद मेरे पास कुछ नहीं बचा था।
after.target: I had nothing left after you left

problem: Grammar and meaning: the Hindi is past (बचा) but the English 'I've got nothing left after you left' mixes present perfect with 'after you left'.
evidence: S0362L03U01 uses the past correctly ('there wasn't much time left after you left'). The target clause 'after you left' is past.

before.known: मेरे पास छुट्टियों के लिए पर्याप्त समय नहीं है।
before.target: I don't have enough time for holidays

after.known: मेरे पास छुट्टियों के लिए काफ़ी समय नहीं है।

problem: R1 ZUT: 'enough' is rendered as पर्याप्त here but as काफ़ी everywhere else in the seed. The known sentence also uses a word the course has not taught.
evidence: S0378L02 maps 'enough money' to काफ़ी पैसे, and seed 378 itself uses काफ़ी for 'enough'.

before.known: मुझे नहीं लगता कि किसी ने मुझे नहीं बताया।
before.target: I don't think that nobody told me

problem: R8: 'I don't think that nobody told me' is a stacked double negative with unnatural meaning (tier 2 or worse).
evidence: S0367L02 'nobody told me' already contains a negation; wrapping it in 'I don't think that' makes the sentence confusing.

before.known: मुझे यक़ीन नहीं है कि किसी ने मुझे नहीं बताया।
before.target: I'm not sure if nobody told me

problem: R8: 'I'm not sure if nobody told me' is clunky and nearly unusable as a natural sentence.
evidence: Sibling B01 'I think nobody told me' and B03 'nobody told me today' are natural. This one stacks a negation on 'not sure if'.
